title: Product safety: safety data sheets, the hazards register and ingredient labels
audience: Makeup artists and makeup businesses that buy, store and use cosmetic and hair products on client work
learningOutcomes: Explain what a safety data sheet is for and where it is kept
Describe the hazards register an employer must keep, and what it lists
Identify a product-use rule from a named source, and state where it applies
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: WorkSafe Victoria, Managing hazardous substances and irritants in the hairdressing and beauty industry (reviewed 12 September 2025); Product Safety Australia, Cosmetics ingredient labelling standard (page dated 22 October 2014). Both are listed in full at the end of the lesson.

instruction.heading: Safety data sheets for every product
instruction.body: A safety data sheet, usually called an SDS, describes the hazards of a product and the controls for using it safely. WorkSafe Victoria states that employers must obtain a current SDS for each hazardous substance or product, normally from the supplier, and that workers who may be exposed must be able to get to it easily. In a makeup kit or a salon, that means a folder or a digital copy that the artist can open at the appointment, not a copy kept only in the office. An SDS can be out of date when a supplier changes a formula. Each time a product is bought in a new formulation, the SDS for that formulation is requested and filed, and the old one is removed from the working set.

instruction.heading: The hazards register
instruction.body: WorkSafe Victoria states that employers must keep a register that lists all the products used at the workplace. For each product the register records the product identifier and the SDS it relates to. The register is a working document. A product that is added to the kit goes on the register before its first use, and a product that is discarded or no longer used is removed with a note of the date. A business that has a register but no current SDS for a listed product has not met the requirement, so the two records have to be checked together.

instruction.heading: Product rules that come from a named source
instruction.body: Some product rules are set out by a named source and must be applied as written. WorkSafe Victoria's guidance on hairdressing and beauty products says that aerosol hair colours must not be used on eyelashes or eyebrows. The same guidance covers products used for eyelash extensions, which are outside this course, and names the controls for their adhesive, including gloves, masks and eye protection. A makeup artist must check the SDS for every product on the kit, and must not apply a product in a way that its SDS or the source rules out. Where a source is silent on a point, the artist does not assume the point is allowed. The artist asks the supplier, or leaves the product out of that service.

instruction.heading: Ingredient labels and the labelling standard
instruction.body: The ACCC, through Product Safety Australia, administers a mandatory cosmetic ingredient labelling standard. The page states that the standard helps consumers identify ingredients they may be allergic or sensitive to, and lets them compare products at the point of sale. The ingredient list on a product is therefore one of the first checks for a client with a known sensitivity. UNCONFIRMED in this draft: the exact format rules of the standard, such as language, order and where the list must appear, which were not read from the current ACCC text. The regulator for chemicals in cosmetic ingredients, the Australian Industrial Chemicals Introduction Scheme, was not reached for this draft. A reviewer must check both before this lesson is approved.

procedure: Check that a current SDS is held for each product on the kit, and that it matches the supplier's current formula
Add each product to the hazards register with its identifier and the SDS it relates to, before the product is first used
Read the SDS control section for each product, and set the controls before the appointment
Check the product's ingredient list against the client's recorded sensitivities before use
Do not use a product for a purpose that its SDS or the named source rules out, and record the decision if a client asks for it
Remove a product from the register when it is discarded, with the date and the reason

workedExamples.situation: An artist is asked to use a hair spray in aerosol form on a client's eyebrows, to hold the brow shape for a photo shoot.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the artist use the spray, and what should be checked?
workedExamples.reasoning: WorkSafe Victoria's guidance says aerosol hair colours must not be used on eyelashes or eyebrows. The artist must not use the product for that purpose. The artist offers a product that is listed for the purpose, with its SDS held, and records the request and the decision.

workedExamples.situation: A new foundation arrives in the same packaging as the old one, but the supplier has issued a new formula.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must happen before the new foundation is used?
workedExamples.reasoning: The SDS on file may describe the old formula. The artist requests the current SDS from the supplier, checks it against the product, updates the hazards register, and only then uses the product. The old SDS is replaced in the working set, and the change is dated.

equipmentAndPpe: Current safety data sheet for each product on the kit
Hazards register listing each product, its identifier and its SDS
Gloves and eye protection where the SDS or the product label requires them

commonErrors.error: Keeping the SDS only in the office, so the artist cannot see it at the appointment.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep a copy in the kit or on a phone or tablet taken to each booking.

commonErrors.error: Filing a product on the register but never requesting its SDS.
commonErrors.prevention: A register entry is complete only when the matching current SDS is held. Check both together.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a product that is sold for one use is safe for every use.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the SDS and the named source for the purpose. Where the source is silent, do not assume the use is allowed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: WorkSafe Victoria states that employers must obtain a current SDS for each hazardous substance or product, and must keep a hazards register of all products used at the workplace. Employers in other states and territories have their own requirements, UNCONFIRMED in this draft.
WorkSafe Victoria states that aerosol hair colours must not be used on eyelashes or eyebrows. This rule applies to the product named in the source only.

This lesson does not give authority to use any product on a client for a purpose beyond its SDS and label. It also does not cover the ingredient-regulation position of the AICIS, which is UNCONFIRMED in this draft.

qualityStandard: Every product on the kit has a current SDS held, and the SDS matches the product's current formula
The hazards register lists every product used, with its identifier and SDS, and is updated when products change
No product is used for a purpose its SDS or named source rules out
documentationEvidence: Hazards register with product identifier and SDS for each product
Dated SDS for each product, with the version or revision date shown
Record of any request for a purpose a product does not cover, and the decision
summary: An SDS is held for each product, is current and is available to the artist at each appointment
The hazards register lists every product used, and must be kept up to date
A product is not used for a purpose its SDS or the named source rules out
The ingredient labelling standard helps clients with sensitivities check products; its format rules are UNCONFIRMED here

knowledgeChecks.question: Under WorkSafe Victoria's guidance, what must an employer hold for each hazardous product?
options: A product brochure from the marketing team
A current safety data sheet that workers who may be exposed can access
A verbal confirmation from the supplier that the product is safe

knowledgeChecks.question: A product is added to the kit and used for the first time next week. When must it go on the hazards register?
options: At the end of the financial year
Only if a client complains about it

knowledgeChecks.question: According to WorkSafe Victoria's guidance, which use must be avoided?
options: Using an aerosol hair colour on eyelashes or eyebrows
Using a moisturiser on the hands before a service
Keeping a product in its original sealed container
